b2-migracion-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Documentary About Brazil
b2-migracion-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about immigration to Brazil, and he asks what you will tell him afterwards.
b2-migracion-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what you will tell him when the documentary ends.
cues: Say when you will tell him
Say which immigrants arrived in Brazil in 1908
b2-migracion-01.target: Cuando termine el documental, te diré que los primeros inmigrantes japoneses llegaron a Brasil en 1908.
b2-migracion-01.english: When the documentary ends, I will tell you that the first Japanese immigrants arrived in Brazil in 1908.
b2-migracion-01.canDo: I can say when something will happen, with *cuando*, *en cuanto* and *hasta que* + subjunctive.

b2-migracion-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Children and School
b2-migracion-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading a report about Venezuelan families in the region, and she asks what you think is most important for children.
b2-migracion-02.prompt: Tell Meg what you think is important for migrant children.
cues: Say what the children should do
b2-migracion-02.target: Es importante que los niños migrantes vayan a la escuela.
b2-migracion-02.english: It is important that migrant children go to school.
b2-migracion-02.canDo: I can say what governments and aid agencies should do, with *es necesario que* and *es importante que* + subjunctive.

b2-migracion-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Whoever Reaches the Border
b2-migracion-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading an article about the border at Cúcuta, and he asks what people there need.
b2-migracion-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what anyone who reaches the border needs.
cues: Say who the sentence is about
b2-migracion-03.target: Cualquier persona que llegue a la frontera necesita información clara.
b2-migracion-03.english: Anyone who reaches the border needs clear information.
b2-migracion-03.canDo: I can talk about any person, place or route, with *cualquiera que*, *quienquiera que* and *dondequiera que* + subjunctive.

b2-migracion-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Money Sent Home
b2-migracion-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are listening to a talk about remittances, and she asks what the economists say.
b2-migracion-04.prompt: Tell Meg what economists say about remittances.
cues: Say what they do not replace
b2-migracion-04.target: Si bien las remesas ayudan a muchas familias, no sustituyen la inversión pública.
b2-migracion-04.english: Although remittances help many families, they do not replace public investment.
b2-migracion-04.canDo: I can grant a point and then make my own, with *si bien* + indicative.

b2-migracion-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Arepas in the Cities
b2-migracion-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading an article about migrants and food, and he asks where you can find Venezuelan food.
b2-migracion-05.prompt: Tell Carlos where Venezuelan arepas are sold.
b2-migracion-05.target: Se venden arepas venezolanas en muchas ciudades de Sudamérica.
b2-migracion-05.english: Venezuelan arepas are sold in many cities of South America.
b2-migracion-05.canDo: I can say what is done, sold or recognised without naming who does it, with *se* + verb.

b2-migracion-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Border Talk
b2-migracion-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are preparing a short talk about borders and migration, and she asks what to say about the Darién.
b2-migracion-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg one fact about the Darién for the talk.
b2-migracion-consolidation.target: Entre Colombia y Panamá está la selva del Darién, y en 2023 la cruzaron más de quinientas mil personas.
b2-migracion-consolidation.english: Between Colombia and Panama lies the Darién jungle, and more than half a million people crossed it in 2023.
b2-migracion-consolidation.canDo: I can use time clauses, value judgments, whoever-clauses, *si bien* and *se* to talk about migration in South America.
